summary: The spine is the most Gate-0-real part of the tree: a durable intent ledger (ledger.py), a kernel-enforced Windows MIC write containment (containment.py), a process-tree cancellation ladder (cancel.py), an absence-means-stop kill switch (killswitch.py), a fail-closed owner-approval verifier (promotion_approval.py) and a registry/conformance contract for effectful entrypoints (effect_boundary.py). Nearly every module carries measured evidence in its docstring and a matching test file, so the slice's health is unusually high per module. The weakness is integration, not code: of the 19 registered entrypoint rows only 1 is Wiring.CENTRAL (python.attempt), 2 are UNGUARDED (python.offload, python.promote_candidates), and the canonical Gate-0 contracts in daedalus/schemas.py (MissionContract, AttemptRecord, EvidencePacket, RuntimeManifest) are imported by nothing in the spine except ContractProvenance -- the live loop runs on its own dataclasses. The single Gate-0 deliverable with NO code anywhere is the Event Store: ADR-011 is still 'Proposed', envelope.py's trace_id is the deliberately minimal join field that landed instead, and grep for EventStore/event_store across daedalus/ returns zero files. daedalus/adapters/ is the weakest sub-slice: a clean adapter/event/transport boundary whose only production consumer is the kairos evolution track, spawning processes with raw asyncio outside cancel.py, containment.py and the kill switch.

modules.purpose: Package docstring plus re-export of the ledger's public names.
issues: Docstring calls the package 'Mission Spine light -- the durable intent ledger' (daedalus/spine/__init__.py:1-7) and re-exports only ledger symbols; the package now also holds the effect-boundary registry, MIC containment, the kill switch and the promotion verifier, none of which are mentioned or exported.
Callers therefore reach every other spine module by submodule import, so the package surface understates the kernel.

modules.purpose: SQLite (WAL) durable intent ledger: intent is committed before the external effect, append-only intent_events, crash window closed by caller-supplied effect_key identification.
modules.plan_mapping: Gate 0 deliverable 1 (event spine, partial: intent ledger only); Invariants 1, 7
issues: It is an INTENT ledger, not the canonical Event Store Gate 0 asks for; ADR-011 (docs/adrs/011-event-spine.md, Status: Proposed) names four unordered durable stores and the unification never landed.

DEFAULT_DB_PATH = <repo>/runs/spine/spine.sqlite3 (ledger.py:118) lives inside the primary checkout -- deliberate and documented, but it means the crash-recovery evidence is inside the tree the attempt is fenced out of.

modules.purpose: TaskAttempt: the one seam that turns a picked task into a gated candidate patch, in an isolated worktree, never touching the primary checkout.
modules.plan_mapping: Gate 0 deliverable 4 (central start path) + Gate 1 attempt isolation; Invariants 3, 5
issues: The ONLY row with wiring=Wiring.CENTRAL in the effect-boundary matrix (effect_boundary.py:249) -- the migration it was meant to lead has not continued.

Imports only ContractProvenance from daedalus.schemas (attempt.py:136): it does not emit the canonical AttemptRecord or EvidencePacket, so the Gate-0 contracts and the live loop are two separate shapes (Invariant 1, one kernel).
No killswitch import anywhere in the module -- a direct run_attempt() call does not consult the permit file; the kill switch is a loop-level concern only (loop.py, atomic.py, build_exec.py).
84 KB single module carrying git choke point, worktree lifecycle, runner protocol, gates, containment call-out, ledger resolution and artifact persistence.

modules.purpose: Deterministic inventory of externally reachable effectful entrypoints plus begin_effect(), which refuses a start whose entrypoint/effects/guard decisions are unknown.
modules.plan_mapping: Gate 0 deliverable 4 (centralized start/guard path) and its conformance evidence; Invariant 8
issues: Measured wiring distribution in the matrix: CENTRAL 2, LOCAL_GUARDS 6, INVENTORY_ONLY 8+ (plus ~40 cli.* rows all INVENTORY_ONLY), UNGUARDED 2, ABSENT 1. Gate 0 cannot close until production-capable rows are CENTRAL.

python.offload (line 290) and python.promote_candidates (line 314) are UNGUARDED with explicit migration notes -- live write providers can mutate the primary checkout; the promotion callable authenticates no owner approval.

begin_effect() consults no kill switch and no spend ledger itself (grep killswitch in this file: no matches); it validates GuardDecisions its caller supplies, so 'enforced at the effect boundary' is true only for rows that were already migrated.
adapter.subprocess row (line 327) is INVENTORY_ONLY: 'cwd/write/egress policy is not centrally leased'.

modules.purpose: Windows MIC (Low integrity) write containment for candidate/gate execution, with bounded single-handle inheritance and an attestation of what was actually achieved.
issues: Explicitly CONFIDENTIALITY: NONE and no network/IPC limit (referenced from attempt.py:475) -- it is write containment, not a sandbox; the plan's 'capability-bounded' isolation is therefore only partly met.
Windows-only mechanism; posix path falls back to the weaker Python-side fences, so the measured guarantee is box-specific.
77 KB module; production callers are attempt.py and health.py only.

modules.purpose: Process-TREE cancellation ladder (graceful CTRL_BREAK/killpg then Job-Object/SIGKILL tree kill), fail-closed if a job cannot be created.
modules.plan_mapping: Gate 0 deliverable 6 (cancellation fixture) + Invariant 8 (kill switch/bounded effects)
issues: Used by attempt/killswitch/health/council/budget/eval but NOT by daedalus/adapters/subprocess_adapter.py, which spawns with raw asyncio and calls process.kill() -- exactly the leaked-grandchild hazard this module's docstring documents.

modules.purpose: Absence-means-stop permit-file kill switch with measured observation/child-death latency bounds and monotonic latching.
modules.plan_mapping: Gate 0 deliverable 5 (kill policy); ADR-016 autonomy precondition; Invariant 8
issues: Consulted by loop.py, atomic.py, build_exec.py and the promotion path -- not by begin_effect() and not by attempt.py, so it is a caller convention rather than an effect-boundary enforcement.
Self-declared hole: an HTTP request already in flight is not aborted; the bound is 'before the next billable call'.

modules.purpose: Measurement-sorted work queue (band + evidence offset) and the review packet behind `daedalus improve`; refuses any candidate without reason/score/evidence.
modules.plan_mapping: Gate 0/1 loop input; no plan section defines the queue -- closest is Gate 8-loop step 3 (selection) in Ariadne
issues: 136 KB, by far the largest module in the slice; sources, scoring, docref candidates, spectral enrichment and rendering all live in one file.
SOURCE_BANDS is an explicitly human PRIOR, not a measurement -- honest, but it means cross-band ranking is policy embedded in the picker rather than in a policy artifact.
Constructs the docref gate argv inline (picker.py:1242) -- the gate command for one work class is defined in the queue rather than in an operator declaration (plan section 9).

modules.purpose: The SHADOW RUN: one iteration of regenerate-sources -> pick -> attempt -> report, which refuses to treat a green gate as evidence and promotes nothing.
modules.plan_mapping: Gate 0 exit evidence / Gate 1 rehearsal; Invariant 5 (sealed promotion)
issues: Its central measured fact -- gate rejection rate 0/3 against known-bad changes -- makes the whole candidate stream 'unproven'; that number is from 2026-07-29 and is a STATUS, not re-measured per revision here (tools/gate_discrimination.py owns the re-measurement).
Explicitly not a loop driver: scheduling/unattended operation is elsewhere, so 'the loop' exists in three places (bootstrap.py, loop.py, kairos/scheduler.py).

modules.purpose: Scans docs for references to code symbols that do not exist, with a conservative module-exists/symbol-missing filter and a resolving/broken measurement PAIR to defeat delete-the-doc gaming.
modules.plan_mapping: Knowledge plane consistency (plan section 5) as a Gate-0-era work source; not itself a Gate-0 deliverable
issues: Exists because the loop's permitted write set (docs/, tests/, README.md) had an empty intersection with the work it wanted to do -- a work source chosen by policy shape rather than by value.
Skips star-import and module-__getattr__ modules wholesale; skips are counted, but coverage is unstated in the headline number.

modules.purpose: The gate a docref candidate is judged by: denominator first, target document still exists and is non-empty, then each dispatched finding; exit 0/1/2 with 'no verdict' separated from 'bad candidate'.
modules.plan_mapping: Gate 0 evidence boundary (Invariant 4: a deterministic evaluator decides)
issues: Landed to fix a measured empty-gate: docref candidates previously carried gate_paths=(doc,) and ran `pytest docs/THAT.md`, so every docref attempt failed for a reason unrelated to the fix.
Deliberately does not check fact preservation (needs the before-image); that half lives in daedalus/verifier.py, so one work class is judged by two modules that must stay in step.

modules.purpose: One ambient trace_id joining six incompatible run-record formats, an in-toto ITE-6 statement() shape, and borrowed OpenTelemetry GenAI attribute names.
modules.plan_mapping: Gate 0 deliverable 1 (event spine) - the minimal substitute for it; Invariant 7 (provenance)
issues: This is the compensating control for the missing Event Store: it explicitly renames nothing and unifies nothing, it only adds a join field (envelope.py docstring, 'It adds ONE field').
GEN_AI borrows names with 'claim no conformance, export nothing' -- no exporter exists, so the observability payoff is deferred.
Adopted by loop/progress/file_bridge/lanes/schemas/storage/picker/attempt, but nothing enforces that a new record producer stamps it.

modules.purpose: Fail-closed verifier for a git-signed promote/<candidate_sha256> tag bound to candidate sha, source revision, evidence sha, expiry and nonce; exit code of git verify-tag is the only authority.
issues: verify_promotion_approval() has NO production caller: the only call sites are tests/test_promotion_approval.py (grep across *.py). The promotion callable it is meant to guard sits in a protected policy artifact, so wiring it requires an amendment.

tests/test_promotion_approval_wiring.py encodes the biconditional (flag True <-> verifier actually called), which keeps the Gate-0 inventory honest but leaves the row UNGUARDED (effect_boundary.py:314).
Trust-root choice is still contested in docs/GATE0_PROMOTION_TRUST_ROOT_CONFLICT.md and docs/AMENDMENT_PROPOSAL_005_PROMOTION_GUARD_ROT.md.

modules.purpose: Public surface for the adapter boundary: AgentAdapter, event types, TransportRecord, sinks, SubprocessAdapter, RUNTIME_PROFILES.
issues: No production module imports the package root; consumers import submodules (daedalus/memory/embeddings.py:93 takes TransportRecord only, daedalus/kairos/shadow_shell.py:6-7 takes base+events).

modules.purpose: Abstract AgentAdapter protocol: capabilities, create_session, send, events, approve, reject, interrupt, terminate.
issues: The plan's Agent Contract is RuntimeManifest in daedalus/schemas.py:1184; this ABC shares no type with it, so the repo has two unconnected 'agent contract' definitions.
No docstring/module header, no capability, egress, workspace, cost or conformance fields -- the Gate-0 contract asks for exactly those.

modules.purpose: Provider-neutral event dataclasses plus the lossless TransportRecord envelope and event_to_transport_record().
issues: TransportRecord carries no trace_id and no cost fields, so adapter traffic cannot be joined to spine records via daedalus/spine/envelope.py.
record_id is derived from session/direction/sequence only; it is not content-addressed, so it is not an artifact identity (Invariant 2).

modules.purpose: TransportSink protocol with in-memory, JSONL and composite implementations.
modules.plan_mapping: Gate 0 deliverable 1 (event store) - a fourth append-only JSONL journal instead
issues: JsonlTransportSink is another unordered, unchained append-only journal -- precisely the class of store ADR-011 was written to unify; no production wiring points at it.
CompositeTransportSink fans out sequentially with no error containment; one failing sink aborts the rest ('failures remain visible' is the stated intent).

modules.purpose: Verified one-shot CLI launch profiles (claude, codex, generic) parsing JSONL into typed events with a timeout and stderr capture.
modules.plan_mapping: Gate 0 deliverable 3/6 (adapter fixtures) - registered UNGUARDED-adjacent as INVENTORY_ONLY at effect_boundary.py:327
issues: Spawns with raw asyncio.create_subprocess_exec and stops with process.kill() (lines ~414-425); it does not use daedalus/spine/cancel.py, so grandchildren survive cancellation on win32 -- the exact hazard cancel.py documents.
No containment: it never calls daedalus/spine/containment.py, so a CLI it launches runs at the caller's integrity level with the caller's write reach.
No begin_effect() call and no kill-switch checkpoint despite declaring PROCESS_SPAWN + NETWORK_EGRESS + FILESYSTEM_WRITE effects.
No cost/spend accounting at all (grep for cost/usd/token: nothing), although Gate 0 requires cost in the adapter fixtures.
approve()/reject() raise NotImplementedError, so the AgentAdapter contract is only partly satisfiable by its only implementation.
Its only production consumer path is daedalus/kairos/evolution.py via shadow_shell.py -- a second candidate-generation route parallel to spine/attempt.py.

docs.reason: Still 'Proposed'. It is the standing record that the Gate-0 Event Store does not exist and that four durable stores remain unordered; envelope.py landed instead. Keep until an Event Store lands or the ADR is superseded.

Accurately describes daedalus/adapters as 'Experimental; transport core partially implemented' and lists what is not implemented (approvals, resume, Ollama). It does not mention that the adapter bypasses spine cancel/containment/effect_boundary, so it understates the gap but does not lie.

The falsifiable gate list that killswitch.py, containment.py and cancel.py were built against; each precondition carries a command or test. It is the local authority for whether the spine may run unattended.
Records the owner's chosen promotion trust root (option B, git-signed tag; option A as migration) that daedalus/spine/promotion_approval.py implements verbatim.
Open conflict record for the same trust root; pairs with docs/AMENDMENT_PROPOSAL_005_PROMOTION_GUARD_ROT.md and explains why promotion_approval.py is still unwired.
Precondition list naming the kill switch and containment as unmet at the time; overlaps ADR-016 and is a merge candidate with it once both sets go green.

integration_gaps: GATE-0 DELIVERABLE WITH NO CODE: the Event Store. grep for EventStore/event_store across daedalus/ returns zero files; ADR-011 is still 'Proposed'. What exists is the intent ledger (spine/ledger.py), three other unrelated journals, and one ambient join field (spine/envelope.py). Nothing assigns a spanning sequence or ordering.

Canonical contracts are an island: MissionContract, AttemptRecord and EvidencePacket appear only in daedalus/schemas.py and tests/test_kernel_contracts.py. daedalus/spine/attempt.py imports only ContractProvenance (attempt.py:136) and returns its own AttemptResult/PatchArtifact, so the Gate-0 schemas do not describe what the live loop actually produces (Invariant 1).

Central start path stalled at one row: python.attempt is the only wiring=Wiring.CENTRAL production row (effect_boundary.py:249). python.offload (line 290) and python.promote_candidates (line 314) are UNGUARDED; ~40 cli.* rows and the whole provider/adapter surface are INVENTORY_ONLY.

begin_effect() enforces nothing about spend or the kill switch itself -- no killswitch reference exists in effect_boundary.py; it validates guard decisions callers hand it. The kill switch is consulted by loop.py/atomic.py/build_exec.py only, so a direct run_attempt() or adapter start is not stoppable through the permit file.

promotion_approval.verify_promotion_approval() has no production caller; the sealed-promotion invariant (5) is implemented and tested but not enforced. The wiring change lands inside a protected policy artifact and needs an amendment.

daedalus/adapters/ bypasses the spine entirely: no begin_effect, no spine.cancel tree kill, no containment labelling, no spend accounting. Its only production route (kairos/shadow_shell.py -> kairos/evolution.py) is a second candidate-generation path beside spine/attempt.py, which weakens the 'one seam' property attempt.py's docstring claims.

Two 'agent contract' definitions coexist: daedalus/adapters/base.py:AgentAdapter (behavioural ABC) and daedalus/schemas.py:1184 RuntimeManifest (the Gate-0 vendor-neutral manifest with conformance receipts). No code connects them, and RuntimeConfig profiles are not hashed into runtime_manifest_sha256.
TransportRecord (adapters/events.py) carries neither trace_id nor cost, so adapter traffic cannot be joined to spine records even through the envelope workaround.
adapters/transport.py JsonlTransportSink adds a further append-only JSONL journal with no chain and no lock -- the same class of store ADR-011 set out to unify.
notable: Stale module docstring: daedalus/spine/__init__.py:1-7 still describes the package as 'Mission Spine light -- the durable intent ledger' and re-exports only ledger names, though the package now contains the effect-boundary registry, MIC containment, the cancellation ladder, the kill switch and the promotion verifier.
daedalus/adapters/base.py has no module docstring at all, and daedalus/adapters/events.py has none either -- the only two files in this slice without the repo's usual measured-evidence header.

daedalus/spine/bootstrap.py's headline claim ('the gate's rejection rate against three known-bad changes was 0/3', hence promotion stays human) is a dated STATUS baked into prose; the live re-measurement lives in tools/gate_discrimination.py, so the docstring can silently age.

Module docstring quality is otherwise exceptionally high and verifiable: attempt.py's four structural no-write properties, containment.py's measured REFUSED/ALLOWED table, killswitch.py's three separate latency bounds with per-run milliseconds, promotion_approval.py's note that `git verify-tag` prints 'Good ... signature' even for a key not in allowed-signers (so only the exit code may be trusted). Spot checks held: DEFAULT_DB_PATH really is runs/spine/spine.sqlite3 (ledger.py:118) and `daedalus improve` really exists (cli.py:72, 1153).
Size concentration: picker.py 137 KB, attempt.py 85 KB, containment.py 77 KB, effect_boundary.py 59 KB -- four files are ~85% of the slice's bytes, and each mixes policy, mechanism and rendering.

containment.py names its own ceiling honestly: CONFIDENTIALITY: NONE, no network or IPC limit, and it refuses the word 'sandbox'. Invariant 3's 'capability-bounded' therefore means write-bounded on win32 only.

tests/test_promotion_approval_wiring.py is a rare construct worth preserving: it asserts a biconditional between the GUARD_CONTRACT_IMPLEMENTED flag and the verifier actually being called, so the Gate-0 inventory cannot be made dishonest in either direction.

Test coverage of this slice is dense -- test_spine_ledger, test_spine_attempt, test_spine_attempt_containment, test_spine_cancel, test_containment, test_gate_containment(+_job_caps), test_killswitch, test_effect_boundary(+_wiring), test_promotion_approval(+_wiring), test_prose_gate, test_docrefs_false_positives, test_envelope_join/_coverage, test_spine_picker, test_picker_work_queue/_outcome, test_shadow_run, test_gate0_faults_atalanta -- so 'unwired' here almost always means unwired, not unproven.
